name: Terra
desc: The one who does not know what she is. Half of something, and nobody will say which half. Moves like she is waiting to be told she is allowed.
provenance_note: MEASURED before this card was written, studio/_tools/known_char_probe.py at seed 9090 on animagine-xl-4.0, evidence at studio/samples/cast/known_terra_probe.jpg. The bare name 'terra branford' returns a BLONDE IN A WHITE HOOD - not her. The danbooru form 'terra branford (final fantasy vi)' reaches the right palette and silhouette and reliably adds an orb held in both hands, which is a noun the tag genuinely carries. But the description-only control lands nearly as close, so the tag is thin and the name is doing less work than its fame suggests. She therefore gets the SAME full build as an invented character - sheet, turnaround, trained LoRA - and the name is used only to seed a better starting portrait. See craft/KNOWN_CHARACTERS.md.
source_note: A character from a published game, so this card records where she comes from. Rendering fan work is ordinary - the danbooru corpus this checkpoint learned from is largely built on it. DISTRIBUTING a finished film built on her is a different question from making one, and it is the author's call to make deliberately rather than by accident. This is not the same as the four blocked voice packs in studio/voices/, which clone real people; those are a likeness question and stay blocked.

note: BUILT AS A TEST OF THE KNOWN-CHARACTER PATH, 2026-08-04. The identity vocabulary is deliberately CONCRETE - green hair, red ribbon, red cape, gold dress, red boots, pointed ears - because the model renders nouns, not adjectives, and an identity resting on 'ethereal' or 'haunted' does not survive a single re-render. The danbooru tag leads the tag string because tag order is load-bearing on the anime path: earlier and more specific wins. The orb the tag likes to add is deliberately NOT in the wear vocabulary - it is a prop, and a prop welded to a character turns up in every shot whether the scene wants it or not, which is the same failure the styles library recorded when a style named after an object put that object in the subject's hands. | REMOVED 'pointed ears' after looking at the first sheet: it produced full elf ears, which is not her design - she reads human in FF6 and the Esper form is a separate thing. A wrong noun is worse here than a missing one because the LoRA would train it in permanently, and every later render would carry ears the card never wanted. Caught at the sheet stage, which is the cheap place to catch it.
status_note: READY, and everything on this card has now been rendered and looked at. She is the project's REFERENCE CHARACTER: what completeness means for a character is whatever this card and that page carry.

costume_note:
FOUR COSTUMES, each with the SAME FIVE DAMAGE LEVELS. Every level names objects and their state rather than a mood, because the model renders nouns: 'battle-worn' renders as nothing, 'one pauldron dented, dried blood on the gauntlet' renders. `wear_tags` at the top level is unchanged and still means the default costume, so every existing card and film is untouched.
CORRECTED 2026-08-04 after the 4x5 grid was actually rendered. This card used to claim damage is ORTHOGONAL to wardrobe - 'armour dents the way a dress tears'. It is not. Court dress, which is defined by a cloth silhouette that survives being torn, is the only costume that lands at all five rungs in every arm at both seeds. Imperial plate, which is defined by hard structure, collapsed to a gown at rungs 3 and 4 - because those rungs were WRITTEN AS REMOVALS ('one pauldron gone', 'breastplate discarded'). Damage is orthogonal for cloth and destructive for structure, and the fix is a writing rule, not a weights change. See costume_text_rule.

style_verdict:
MEASURED ACROSS THE WHOLE LIBRARY, 2026-08-04: all 92 status=ready style cards on both engines, 250 cells, two seeds, every cell opened. Tool studio/_tools/terra_styles.py, machine-readable result studio/samples/cast/terra_styles/verdicts.json, 70 contact sheets beside it. This field previously recorded a five-style probe and understated what is known.
THE COMPOSITION HIJACK AND THE IDENTITY FAILURE ARE ONE FAILURE. Where a style wins the framing and pushes her back in the frame, her hair is repainted RED with it. A character LoRA holds identity in proportion to the pixels the character occupies, so 'the style shrank her' and 'the style repainted her' are the same event. 11 of 66 anime cells failed at seed 3311 and about 40 at 7788, and at 7788 almost every failing cell is one where she is small. Pinning 'cowboy shot' first in the tag string fixes it at one seed and fails at another - it is not seed-robust.
THREE ARMS, NO FREE OPTION (sheet_hair_01..03.jpg, 33 cells, unanimous): 0.50 + no name gives full style strength and red hair; 0.50 + name gives green hair and drags Amano canon back, a feathered headdress on no card of hers and a bandeau replacing her dress; 0.85 + no name gives green hair AND the right costume and visibly weakens the style. Default 0.50 / no name, escalate to 0.85 for the named failures, never restore the tag.
THE QWEN EDIT-REF PATH DOES NOT HAVE THIS PROBLEM: 28 of 29 hold at the second seed, because pixel conditioning beats a weight-space prior when something else is fighting for the frame. A style that changes how she is DRAWN lands completely there; a style that needs to change what she IS (pixar_3d, claymation, stop_motion_felt) converts the set and leaves her a photographic human in it.
SHORTLIST, strong AND holding at both seeds: anime - ova_80s, watercolour, cel_anime_90s, golden_age_illustration, retro_shoujo_70s, art_nouveau, psychedelic_60s, pop_art, manga_inked, manga_screentone, oil_painting, pixel_art, wuxia, y2k_chrome, vaporwave, idol_bright, kyoani_soft, art_deco, american_comic, charcoal_drawing, pencil_sketch, shonen_action, modern_anime. qwen - neo_noir, cyberpunk_neon, cinestill_night, street_bw, infrared_photo, polaroid, long_exposure_night, cross_processed, cyanotype, kodachrome, noir_comic, blueprint, pointillism, eight_bit, cinematic_film_still.

photo_prose: a close portrait at 50mm and f/1.8 of a young woman in her early twenties, oval face with a soft jaw, straight nose, wide-set grey-green eyes under level dark brows, pale skin. Her hair is a saturated deep green, long and loose. One hard source high and camera-right, a crisp shadow edge running down the cheek, the rest of the frame falling to black. She wears a heavy raw-silk tabard in faded ochre with a woven red and indigo border, a soft wool cape in dull carmine pinned at one shoulder, a wide belt of worn brown leather, and tall scuffed brown boots. sheet_photo_verdict: REPLACED AGAIN 2026-08-05, the second replacement, after the user rejected the realistic version twice. Tool studio/_tools/terra_real.py, 121 renders, every contact sheet looked at. THE FAULT WAS NOT THE PROMPT DOWNSTREAM, IT WAS THE SHEET'S OWN SURFACE. The v1 composite was itself made through the qwen EDIT path, so its skin was the smooth poreless surface that path produces, and because the sheet pins medium and surface as hard as it pins identity, every photoreal render of her inherited that smoothness. The evidence was already sitting in terra_photo_face.jpg and had been read only half way: arm D, the no-sheet control, was dismissed as the wrong woman and never credited as the only genuinely photographic cell in the strip. THE FIX IS THAT THE FACE PANEL IS BORN ON THE T2I PATH, where the skin is real, and is never round-tripped through the edit path. Both panels of v2 are one person by construction - the body panel is generated FROM the winning face portrait, which the v1 composite was not: its two panels were two independently generated women hstacked together, and their jaws do not match. Evidence: studio/samples/cast/terra_real/01_portraits_*.jpg (30 cells, hair x light), 02_moods_*.jpg (30, grade x expression), 03_finals_noribbon.jpg, 04_bodies_threequarter.jpg, 05_sheets.jpg, 06_probe_close.jpg / _hall.jpg / _street.jpg. v1 is preserved as sheet_photo_terra_v1.png; sheet_photo_terra.png now holds the same bytes as v2 so that the tools which build the filename by convention rather than reading this field agree with it.
voice_verdict: CAST female_04_maya, MEASURED 2026-08-04. Eight castable voices read the SAME LINE of hers at one seed on one engine, evidence at studio/samples/cast/terra_voice/ with audition_sheet.png and every number in measurements.json. WHAT THE ALTERNATIVES SOUNDED LIKE. female_03_alice is the obvious casting and it is WRONG, for a reason that has nothing to do with the audio: NIKA already has it, and NIKA's card reads 'Has never once been asked what she wants' against Terra's 'waiting to be told she is allowed'. Two characters with the same brief and the same reference wav are one character. Alice also came back hot - peak -0.4 dBFS, rms -17.3, the second-loudest of the eight - which is a confident read, and Terra is not confident. female_01 was the FASTEST of the eight, 5.64s against a 6.7s median for the same 22 words, and the flattest at 5.2 semitones; fast plus flat reads as closed and brisk, which is the opposite of someone trailing off. female_02 had the widest range at 12.3 semitones and the longest pauses at 0.51s - it declaims, it lands each clause like a finding, and it is already the wrong shape before you reach the meaning. mabel was the brightest thing measured, centroid 3209 Hz and rolloff to 6146, and brightness reads as sparkle. en_woman sat high at 229 Hz and clones off a 6.4s reference, the second-weakest source in the library. vex and belinda were controls at the edges and behaved as controls should. WHAT DECIDED IT. Three things, in order. (1) TIMBRE: maya came back the darkest of the eight by a wide margin - centroid 1719 Hz against a 2013-3209 field, rolloff 2980 against 3461-6146. Dark is the sound of someone holding their voice down, and that is the character. (2) IT DOES NOT PUSH: peak -6.8 dBFS and rms -24.9, the quietest read of the eight except mabel, and it keeps 19% silence with shaped decaying phrase ends rather than running on. A voice with air in it can be interrupted, and Terra is a person who expects to be. (3) IT IS THE ONLY REFERENCE LONG ENOUGH TO CLONE PROPERLY: 27.2s, inside the 24-30s band the pack recommends. Every other candidate here is 5.9-10.2s. That is not a taste judgement, it is the difference between a stable clone and a lottery, and it will matter more on a feature than on one line. THE COST, STATED: maya's own voice card says avoid for shouting, and that turned out to be true and fixable - see voice_direction.
voice_engine_verdict: indextts2, NOT the house engine, and this is the one place Terra departs from the rest of the cast. BRACK, MANAGER, NIKA, RASK and VIRO are all higgs_v3. MEASURED, same voice, same four lines, same seeds, both engines, sheets at lines_higgs_sheet.png and lines_indextts2_sheet.png. HIGGS_V3 HAS NO DYNAMICS. Across dialogue, whisper, shout and strain its output sat between rms -23.8 and -25.7 dBFS - the whisper and the shout are 1.3 dB apart, which is nothing. It moved PITCH for the shout (236 -> 267 Hz), so it reads the punctuation as intonation, but the level never changes: it performs the WORDS of a shout in a speaking voice. Look at lines_higgs_sheet.png and all four waveforms are the same size. On IndexTTS-2 with the vector the same four lines spread 6.2 dB and the waveform ladder is visible at a glance. AND INDEXTTS-2 IS CLOSER TO HER. On the one line rendered identically on both, the reference wav measures 197.2 Hz median / 1820 Hz centroid; IndexTTS-2 with an all-zero vector returned 201.8 Hz / 1819 Hz, and higgs_v3 returned 235.9 Hz / 1964 Hz. IndexTTS-2 lands within 0.4 semitones and 1 Hz of the source. That is one matched line, not a sweep, so treat the size of the gap as provisional - but it points the same way as the dynamics finding and nothing points the other way. WHAT IT COSTS: IndexTTS-2 needs descript-audiotools and ComfyUI/temp to exist, and renders in ~3-20s a line against ~3-5s for higgs. Cheap. WHAT IT BUYS EVEN WITH THE VECTOR AT ZERO - which is all compile.py can currently emit - is that the route exists. A character on higgs_v3 can never be directed by anything except her own punctuation.
voice_direction: MEASURED CEILINGS ON THE EMOTION VECTOR, and they are not the same for every dimension. studio/samples/cast/terra_voice/emotion_sweep_sheet.png, one voice, one line, one seed, two dimensions, five values each. ANGRY BREAKS HER BETWEEN 0.4 AND 0.6. Median pitch by value: 0.2 -> 199 Hz (i.e. nothing, the neutral read is 202), 0.4 -> 229 Hz, 0.6 -> 360 Hz, 0.8 -> 464 Hz, 1.0 -> 494 Hz. A 197 Hz voice at 494 Hz is not angry, it is a different person - and 0.8 also came back peaking at -0.13 dBFS, i.e. against the ceiling. On the spectrogram the harmonic stack is clean at 0.2 and 0.4 and smears into broad bands from 0.6 up. USE 0.4 AS THE HARD MAX ON ANGRY. AFRAID IS WELL BEHAVED AND SATURATES AT 0.8. By value: 0.2 -> 187 Hz, 0.4 -> 210, 0.6 -> 223, 0.8 -> 260, 1.0 -> 260. The 0.8 and 1.0 renders are the SAME WAVEFORM - correlation r = +1.000 - so the dimension clamps and anything above 0.8 is wasted typing. Nothing clipped, the phrase gaps stayed open, the harmonics stayed legible at every value. AFRAID IS USABLE TO 0.8. THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE LoRA FINDING and should be read that way: a strength knob at its maximum destroys the thing it is modulating. 0.85 collapsed NIKA's field to a grey void and Terra's snow forest to flat beige; 1.0 on Angry collapses her voice to a shriek. The difference is that on audio the safe value is per-dimension, so it needs sweeping per dimension - only Angry and Afraid have been measured here. Happy, Sad, Surprised, Disgusted, Calm and Melancholic are UNMEASURED. HOW TO GET EACH REGISTER OUT OF HER, all four rendered and kept: dialogue = vector all zero, let the text do it. whisper = Afraid 0.4 plus a text that is actually a whisper; do not expect the engine to invent one. shout = Angry 0.4, which returns 305 Hz and rms -18.3 against a -25.4 neutral. That is a RAISED VOICE, not a scream, and it is the honest ceiling: the first pass at Angry 0.9 gave a louder result and lost her completely at 408 Hz. Kept as evidence at lines_indextts2_unbounded/. If a scene genuinely needs Terra screaming, that is a casting problem to solve with a second reference wav, not a slider to push. strain = Afraid 0.8, which returns 309 Hz and rms -19.5 with the phrasing intact.

voice_lines.note: RAW, deliberately not loudness-normalised, so level differences between registers are real. short.py normalises film lines to -18 LUFS with a compressor in front, which would flatten this ladder to nothing.

voice_audition.line: I don't know what I am. Nobody will say it out loud. And I stopped asking, because asking makes them look away.
voice_audition.note: The four blocked packs clone real identifiable people and are not reachable from this tool by construction - cast_voice.py refuses any voice whose card is not status ready, verified by trying it. The unsupported packs are rejected by UnifiedTTSTextNode itself.

voice_library_verdict: A FINDING ABOUT THE VOICE LIBRARY, not about Terra, recorded here because this is where it was measured. THE CARDS DESCRIBE THE REFERENCE WAV, NOT THE RENDER, and the two differ in ways that will mis-cast the next character. PITCH DOES NOT SURVIVE CLONING. Reference median -> higgs_v3 clone median, from the same audition: belinda 256 -> 218, vex 248 -> 205, mabel 256 -> 231, en_woman 218 -> 229, female_02 186 -> 165. Everything is dragged toward a 165-231 Hz band. Casting on the Hz figure in a voice card is casting on a number the engine will not honour. PACE DOES NOT SURVIVE EITHER, AND ONE CARD SAYS IT DOES. vex.json warns that at 2.35 onsets/sec it is 'roughly half the speed of every other voice here' and that 'the drawl is baked into the reference and clones inherit it'. MEASURED: the vex clone read the 22-word audition line in 6.52s at 5.20 onsets/sec - mid-pack, and FASTER than belinda, mabel, female_02 and maya. The drawl did not clone. The warning on vex.json, and the doubt it casts on VIRO's casting, are both wrong on this engine. WHAT DOES SURVIVE IS RELATIVE TIMBRE. mabel stayed the brightest (centroid 3209, rolloff 6146), maya stayed the darkest (1719/2980), female_02 kept the widest pitch range (12.3 st) and female_01 the narrowest (5.2 st) - the same ordering the cards describe. SO: cast on timbre and relative range, which transfer. Do not cast on absolute pitch or onsets/sec, which do not. ALSO: raw engine output is NOT level-matched. Across eight voices, peak ran -0.4 to -8.6 dBFS and rms -15.5 to -24.9, a 9.4 dB spread with three voices arriving at -0.4 dBFS. Any film mixing two characters must normalise, which short.py does.
voice_emotion_routing: IS THE EMOTION LIBRARY WIRED TO TTS? NO - AND IT IS ONE MAPPING AWAY FROM BEING SO. Precisely: all 27 cards in studio/emotions/ are status 'partial' and every one carries voice_style and voice_rate. compile.py:719 emits a warning per beat saying the voice_style 'is not routed to TTS yet', and that warning is accurate about the STUDIO. It is not evidence about the ENGINE, and the two were never separated. THE ENGINE HALF WORKS, MEASURED. Same voice, same line, same seed, only the IndexTTS-2 vector moving: all-zero gave 202 Hz / rms -25.4; Afraid 1.0 gave 260 Hz / -21.7; Angry 1.0 gave 494 Hz / -11.7; Sad 1.0 gave 223 Hz / -28.4 with 42% silence and a 26.7-semitone range. That is up to 292 Hz of pitch and 13.7 dB of level from the vector alone. The slider is not wired to nothing. Evidence: emotion_probe_sheet.png. WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING IS TWO THINGS, AND ONLY ONE IS BUILDABLE. (1) voice_style IS AN ADJECTIVE AND THE ENGINE TAKES NAMED DIMENSIONS. The 27 cards carry 26 distinct words - hollow, wistful, guarded, clipped, flustered, roaring. IndexTTS-2 takes eight named floats: Happy Angry Sad Surprised Afraid Disgusted Calm Melancholic. There is no path from one to the other except a hand-written mapping table, which is the same lesson the image half of this project keeps learning - the model renders nouns, not adjectives, and 'hollow' is an adjective. A draft mapping for all 27 is in studio/_tools/cast_voice.py as EMOTION_MAP, unrendered and unverified; it is a starting point, not a measurement. (2) voice_rate HAS NOTHING TO MAP TO. All 27 cards carry a rate from 0.75 to 1.35 and IndexTTSEngineNode as installed exposes NO speech-rate or duration input at all - checked against /object_info, the inputs are emotion_alpha, temperature, top_p, top_k, length_penalty, num_beams, repetition_penalty, max_mel_tokens, interval_silence and housekeeping. AUDIO.md sells IndexTTS-2 on 'precise duration control - you can force a line to fit an exact number of seconds'; that capability is real upstream and is NOT exposed by this node pack. So voice_rate is currently unroutable, and pretending otherwise would put a number in a workflow that silently does nothing. AND THE THIRD PIECE, WHICH IS NOT IN THE EMOTION LIBRARY AT ALL: compile.py builds its voices map as engine plus wav only, so even a finished mapping has no channel to travel down. short.py:598 already reads cfg['emotion'] and applies it - the consumer exists and the producer does not. That is a one-line-shaped gap in a file this task does not own.

voice_spec._: WHAT A COMPLETE CHARACTER'S AUDIO SECTION CONTAINS. Terra is the reference character, so this is the template every later character inherits and the list the dossier page should render as a checklist. Ten fields; she now has nine. The principle is the same one the image half runs on: a claim on a card is worthless until something was rendered and looked at, so every field below either names a rendered artefact or names the measurement that justifies it.
voice_spec.1_voice: REQUIRED. '<engine> <path/to/reference.wav>'. The format compile.py splits on whitespace. Must resolve to a voice card whose status is 'ready' - never 'blocked' (real people) and never 'unsupported' (the node rejects the path mid-render).
voice_spec.2_voice_verdict: REQUIRED. WHY this voice, naming the alternatives and what they sounded like. A cast decision with no losing candidates in it is not reusable by the next character. Must also record collisions: who else in the cast already has this wav.
voice_spec.3_voice_audition: REQUIRED. The evidence. One line - the CHARACTER'S OWN line, not a neutral sentence - through every plausible candidate at one seed on one engine, plus the sheet and the numbers. Held seed and held engine are what make the comparison mean anything.
voice_spec.4_voice_engine_verdict: REQUIRED where the character departs from the house engine, and worth stating even where she does not. Which engine, and what was measured to choose it.
voice_spec.5_voice_direction: REQUIRED. The MEASURED ceiling on every emotion dimension used, and which dimensions are still unmeasured. This is the audio equivalent of lora_strength_measured and it is per-dimension, not one number.
voice_spec.6_voice_lines: REQUIRED. A rendered set covering the registers the character will actually be asked for - at minimum dialogue, whisper, shout, strain - kept RAW so the dynamic ladder is visible, with the direction that produced each one recorded next to it.
voice_spec.7_voice_range_note: REQUIRED. What this voice CANNOT do, measured rather than assumed. Terra cannot scream without ceasing to be Terra. A character sheet that only lists capabilities will get a director halfway into a scene before the limit shows up.
voice_spec.8_soundscape: MISSING FOR EVERYONE, INCLUDING TERRA. The libraries already exist - 8 soundscapes, 20 sfx cards including cloth_movement, footsteps_concrete, footsteps_grass, metal_clang and breath, and 22 music cues - and NOT ONE of the seven character cards references any of them (checked: the only hit is the English word 'cue' in VIRO's motion_verdict). A character has sounds that belong to her and are not her voice, and Terra's are already decided by data that exists: her costumes map says imperial plate, which is metal_clang and a different footstep from the court dress. This is the largest remaining hole in the audio half and it is NOT filled by this task.
voice_spec.9_voice_processing: OPTIONAL. The ffmpeg filter chain for a character heard through something - radio, helmet, water, memory. short.py already honours a per-character `filter` key on the film's voices map and no character card has ever set one.
voice_spec.10_theme: OPTIONAL. A named music cue that belongs to the character, from the 22 already in studio/cues/. Nothing in the project links a character to a cue today.
voice_spec.verification_standard: State plainly, on every card, what was checked BY EAR and what was only measured. This card was measured and looked at as waveform and spectrogram, and every render was passed through ASR to prove the words are present. NONE OF IT WAS HEARD. That standard should be written down rather than left for a reader to assume either way.
voice_spec.0_why_this_list_exists: THE APP DOES NOT COUNT AUDIO AS PART OF A COMPLETE CHARACTER. Verified at studio/cast.html:351: the green 'complete - sheet, turnaround, trained weights, own clothes' badge is computed from lora_exists AND sheet_exists AND views AND wear_tags, and the voice is not in the test. The page does warn about a MISSING voice and refuses a BLOCKED one, which is the safety half and it works - but a character carrying a bare wav filename with no audition, no direction, no measured ceiling and no rendered line reads as 100% done. Terra scored complete before this task started and her voice field was null. That is the gap this spec closes, and closing it properly means the completeness test learns about the fields below.

voice_range_note: WHAT SHE CANNOT DO. She cannot scream. Angry 0.4 is the measured ceiling before the clone stops being her, and 0.4 buys a raised voice at 305 Hz and rms -18.3 - loud enough for 'get away from her', not loud enough for a death scene. maya's own voice card predicted this in the words 'avoid for high emotion, shouting'; the sweep put a number on it. She also has no bottom: the reference sits at 197 Hz and no dimension measured here moved her DOWN more than 10 Hz, so a low, dangerous register is not available at any setting. Both limits are consistent with the character and neither was chosen for that reason.
voice_note: WHAT WAS AND WAS NOT VERIFIED, stated plainly because the difference matters. VERIFIED: 33 renders, every one measured for duration, peak, rms, crest, clipped samples, silence fraction, longest pause, lead and tail silence, median and 10th/90th-percentile pitch, semitone range, voiced fraction, spectral centroid, 85% rolloff, flatness and onset rate - all in measurements.json. Every one plotted as waveform and mel spectrogram on shared axes and LOOKED AT; that is how the harmonic smear above Angry 0.4 was caught, and it is not visible in the numbers alone. Every one transcribed by the Granite ASR already on the box and scored against the line it was asked for: ALL 33 CAME BACK AT WORD ERROR RATE 0.000, including the 494 Hz Angry 1.0 render. No file was silent, truncated, clipped or empty. NOT VERIFIED: none of it was heard. There are no ears on this box and no agent has any. ASR is a strong test that the words are present and it is not a test of whether a read is good - a flat, dead, technically perfect delivery scores 0.000 exactly like a great one. It also could not choose between the eight candidates, because all eight scored 0.000; the casting was decided on timbre, level, phrasing and reference length, which are proxies. A human should play the four files in voice_lines before this voice goes into a finished film, and should specifically listen for whether maya's technical-narrator register reads as CAREFUL, which is what it was cast for, or as merely BLAND, which is the failure mode a spectrogram cannot distinguish.
lora_previous: character_terra_00001_.safetensors is the ORIGINAL uncaptioned LoRA and is KEPT in models/loras, with a byte copy at character_terra_00001_.safetensors.keep. character_terra_00001_v2.safetensors is the intermediate step - recaptioned, single costume. Both are superseded by v3 but retained so any claim here can be re-measured rather than taken on trust. lora_training_note: TRAINED FROM CAPTIONED PAIRS, which is the thing that changed. The first LoRA was trained on captions reading 'terra, front' and nothing else. In training, whatever a caption NAMES stays separable and whatever it omits is absorbed into the trigger - so 'terra' silently came to mean the woman AND her gold dress AND the flat taupe wall she was photographed against. Captions now name the trigger, the view, the garments at damage level 0, and the backdrop; they still do NOT name hair, eyes or face, because those are the character and should stay welded on. The dataset also spans TWO costumes so no single garment appears in every image. See craft/TRAINING_CAPTIONS.md.
lora_costume_verdict:
MEASURED, studio/samples/cast/terra_costume_fix/costume_baseline.jpg and costume_ab.jpg and costume_mixed_ab.jpg - all four costumes at wear 0, one seed, one place, full body. THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS WAS ONLY HALF RIGHT. The baseline grid adds the control the first pass omitted - the same shot with NO LoRA at all - and it splits the blame:
  danbooru name + no LoRA  -> imperial plate LANDS, full black armour
  danbooru name + LoRA     -> plate FAILS, the patterned dress persists underneath
  name stripped + LoRA     -> plate LANDS
  name stripped + no LoRA  -> plate LANDS
The tag 'terra branford (final fantasy vi)' carries her canonical outfit in the base checkpoint, and the LoRA carried it too. EITHER ONE ALONE IS SURVIVABLE; THE TWO TOGETHER SATURATE and the costume loses. Retraining fixed the LoRA's half - at v3 with the name still in the prompt the court dress finally arrives with its white gloves and embroidered hem, and the plate reads as actual metal rather than painted fabric - but the tag's half is a PROMPT problem and cannot be trained away. For a costume shot on a known character, strip the danbooru name; the LoRA carries her without it, which was already measured in her original lora_verdict column 4.
PER COSTUME at v3, name still in the prompt: traveller LANDS (it is the trained default). court LANDS. armour PARTIAL - metal is present, a sash and skirt persist. field FAILS. With the name stripped: traveller, court and armour all LAND, field still FAILS.
FIELD IS NOT A TRAINING PROBLEM AT ALL and no retrain will touch it. Its own level-0 wear_tags read 'heavy brown travelling coat OVER THE GOLD DRESS'. The model renders nouns, so it renders the gold dress and drops the coat - the costume names the very garment it is supposed to replace. It failed identically in all four rows including both no-LoRA controls. That is a card authoring fix, not a weights fix.
lora_setting_verdict:
MEASURED, studio/samples/cast/terra_costume_fix/setting_grid.jpg, two places at 0.50 and 0.85, v1 against v3. '0.85 DESTROYS THE SETTING' WAS NEVER A PROPERTY OF STRENGTH. Every turnaround view is shot against the same flat taupe wall and the original captions named it nowhere, so the trigger absorbed the wall exactly as it absorbed the dress. Turning the LoRA up turned the memorised wall up - and 'collapsed to flat beige' is that wall, literally, at its own colour. Confirmed and then fixed: v1 at 0.85 replaces the snow forest with a featureless taupe void and reduces the meadow to a small arch-shaped window in a taupe field. v3, whose captions say 'plain flat grey background', holds a real forest with trees and depth and a real meadow with grass, flowers and sky at the same 0.85 and the same seed.
So the strength ceiling is raised. lora_strength_measured stays 0.5 because that is what every existing shot and film was built against and it remains correct; 0.85 is now available for shots that want a harder identity lock, measured in two places rather than the whole places library.
costume_text_rule:
TWO RULES FOR WRITING A COSTUME LADDER, both MEASURED on this character and both expected to hold for every character in the project. Evidence: studio/samples/cast/terra_wardrobe/field_fix_{name,noname}_s{4242,1337}.jpg and damage_nouns_{name,noname}_s{4242,1337}.jpg, tools studio/_tools/field_fix.py and studio/_tools/damage_nouns.py.
1. NEVER NAME THE GARMENT THE COSTUME EXISTS TO REPLACE. The field coat's level 0 read 'heavy brown travelling coat OVER THE GOLD DRESS'. The model renders nouns, so it rendered the gold dress and dropped the coat - in all four LoRA/name arms at both seeds. Removing four words puts the coat on her in 4 of 4 arms. This was diagnosed independently by two agents from the two rungs that already worked and neither tested it; it is now a measurement.
2. WRITE DAMAGE AS A DAMAGED THING, NOT AS A MISSING THING. 'gone', 'missing', 'discarded' give the sampler nothing to draw and it falls back on whatever the trigger and the danbooru tag already know, which is the default costume. Rewriting the same state as objects that are present - 'dented steel breastplate buckled at the ribs, one steel pauldron, torn mail sleeves' - brought real metal, gauntlets and greaves back at plate rung 3 in both seeds, and put the torn coat back on her at field rung 3. HONEST LIMIT: plate rung 4 only partly recovers. It gains the red tabard and loses the plain cocktail dress, but the mail does not reliably arrive - at some point a ladder really has run out of costume, and rung 4 is close to it.
SHARPENED by auditing the rest of the cast against the rule. Rule 2 is NOT 'never write the word gone'. Terra's own court dress says 'circlet gone' at rung 2 and 'both gloves gone' at rung 3, and the court dress lands at ALL FIVE rungs in every arm at both seeds - because those rungs still NAME A GARMENT THAT IS PRESENT ('green gown with a torn hem', 'green gown torn to the knee'). The rungs that failed named only removals and left nothing to draw. So the test to apply to a rung is not 'does it contain a removal', it is 'after the removals, is anything still named'. The whole cast was checked with this: only TERRA has a costumes map at all, and PIP's single wear ladder is subtractive at all five rungs and is the next one to look at.
view_verdict:
MEASURED, studio/_tools/terra_views.py, 160 renders, studio/samples/cast/terra_views/. A TURNAROUND CANNOT BE ASKED FOR IN DEGREES ON THE QWEN EDIT PATH. 'Rotate the camera N degrees clockwise' is read as an IMAGE transform: nine of 24 cells came back rolled 90 degrees and six drew her twice (sheet_yaw_rotate_failed.jpg, kept as evidence). The orbit phrasing never rolls, and the NUMBER is inert - 24 steps around a full circle produced 24 near-identical three-quarter poses, similarity 0.931-0.980 with no trend. NAMED VIEWS WORK and give a textbook V curve, front 1.000 -> back 0.836 -> front_3q_r 0.948 (sheet_octants.jpg). That set is the reference asset to hand an animator.
HANDEDNESS COLLAPSES AT FULL FIGURE: profile_l and profile_r both face screen-left, back_3q_l and back_3q_r are both plain back views - 4 distinct angles from 8 requested. Her own 16-view training set DOES separate left from right, and its phrasing is a HEAD turn at a close crop rather than a body instruction at full body. ELEVATION HAS THREE STOPS, NOT FIVE: low and high angle land with real foreshortening; 'worm eye' and 'bird eye' are re-read as camera DISTANCE and come back eye-level with her smaller. Framing words in an edit prompt are a suggestion - 23 of 24 yaw cells ignored their pinned shot size, because the SOURCE sheet is full figure.
frame_verdict:
MEASURED, studio/samples/cast/terra_views/sheet_frames.jpg, six shot sizes x three seeds on the production path. THE HONEST CUT-OFF FOR A SHOT THAT MUST READ AS TERRA IS 5_wide - full body, whole figure in frame. At 6_full she is a few dozen pixels at the end of a hall, has no face, and the costume is INVENTED (a red bodice with a long train at one seed, a red-and-gold gown at another). Treat 6_full as a silhouette shot: green hair and red-and-gold, nothing more.
THE MOST REPRODUCIBLE SHOT SIZE IS THE COWBOY SHOT (cross-seed 0.938) and reproducibility falls off at BOTH ends - the extreme close-up is 0.903, not the safest crop, because at that size the costume is out of frame and the seed is free to redesign the eye styling, which it visibly does at one of three seeds.
emotion_verdict:
MEASURED, all 27 emotion cards x 2 seeds on the production path, studio/samples/cast/terra_views/sheet_emotions_s4242.jpg and _s7411.jpg. TWENTY ARE DIRECTABLE and read as the same woman doing legibly different things. Most repeatable: smug, tender, shock, focus. Furthest from neutral while still being her: joy, then determined, then resolve.
RAGE REBUILDS HER FACE AND DOES IT AT BOTH SEEDS - the lowest vs-neutral score of all 27 by four points. Cropped and looked at: large soft green almond eyes become small round pupils in huge white sclera, the skin goes from pale pink to flat mid-brown as the card's 'red face' tag repaints the whole head, the jaw widens. Hair, headpiece and earrings are untouched, which is why a broken cell still scans as Terra at thumbnail size. USE angry, NEVER rage.
SEVEN CARDS FAIL AND FOUR FAIL BY ONE MECHANISM: despair, relief, shame and awe carry `body` tags describing a WHOLE-FIGURE posture ('hunched, collapsed', 'head back'), which at wear 0 goes into the prompt and overrides the pinned 'portrait, upper body' - the shot re-frames itself and the face is lost. awe at seed 7411 threw her head so far back the face is entirely out of frame. These are the cards a director most wants for a reaction shot. compose.py:2074 already has this check for an emotion's MOUTH tag against the shot and has no equivalent for its BODY tag.
place_verdict: MEASURED, 18 places spanning all six families at one seed each, studio/samples/cast/terra_wardrobe/places_grid.jpg and places_faces.jpg. She survives all 18. READ THE CAVEAT BEFORE USING THIS: one seed per place manufactures false failures at roughly one in six. floating_islands came back with CORAL hair and would have been written down as a property of the place; re-rendered at six seeds it is green in five (11.9 / 79.0 / 52.7 / 35.9 / 64.8 / 28.2 percent green in the head crop) and only the sweep's own seed is coral. Evidence recheck_floating_islands.jpg. A one-seed library sweep is a screening pass, not a verdict on any single card.
motion_verdict:
MEASURED FROM FRAME STRIPS, nine clips, studio/samples/cast/terra_motion/. NOTHING WAS WATCHED AS VIDEO - there are no eyes on this box. IDENTITY IS NOT BUDGETED BY TIME, IT IS BUDGETED BY WHETHER THE ACTION TURNS HER AWAY. walk_in at market_street holds her frontal and stable for the full 8.04s - the clean confirmation that identity survives 8s at strength 0.5. head_turn at snowfield is frontal through 6.00s then breaks hard between 6s and 7s and is back-of-head by 8s. turn_away loses the face at 4s. step_back OVER-DELIVERS: she recedes to a quarter of her starting height by 4s - it is a walk-away, not a step.
A PLACE WITH A STRONG IMPLIED PROP CAN CAPTURE A GESTURE: hand_to_face at library_reading_room did not complete, because LTX put a red book in her hands and her hands went to the book. The hand_to_face card's own verdict says the gesture completes at all four stagings - it was measured across stagings, never across PLACES. The character LoRA is not in the video graph at all.
identity_note:
TWO THINGS THE IDENTITY VOCABULARY SAYS THAT THE RENDERS DO NOT, both left DELIBERATELY UNFIXED because changing `tags` would move every render of her and invalidate the LoRA that was trained against them. Recorded here so nobody rediscovers them as bugs.
1. THE HEADPIECE IS NOT A RED RIBBON. The tags say 'red hair ribbon'. All 160 view renders and the sheets on both engines draw a large pink-and-gold ornament with a red gem and two upswept prongs that read as HORNS. It is in the source sheet, so both engines inherit it, and it is now trained into the LoRA. This is the same class of problem as the 'pointed ears' that were caught and removed at the sheet stage - except this one was not caught. Fixing it means a new sheet and a retrain, not a tag edit.
2. THE BODICE COLOUR IS UNSTABLE ON THE PRODUCTION PATH. The card says 'sleeveless gold dress with red and blue pattern'. Across the framing ladder and the emotion grid the bodice flips between gold-with-spots and red-with-florals seed by seed and even cell by cell at the same seed. The costume work fixed which GARMENT arrives; this is the garment's COLOUR, a different bug, and it is live in every shot.
3. THE TWO ENGINES DISAGREE ABOUT HER HAIR: a saturated teal-green on the qwen edit path, a pale yellow-mint on the anime production path, consistently. Measured off a render, that hair is median hue 110 at SATURATION 46 - less than half what a naive 'is it green' threshold assumes, which is how one measurement pass reported her hair leaving frame while it filled a quarter of it.

RESOLVED 2026-08-15 (Phase 4 evidence pass): prose corrected to the ornament; tags kept byte-identical because the LoRA captions never named the headpiece, so it lives in the trigger and the tag is inert on the anime engine. See `headpiece`.
setting_verdict: CORRECTED 2026-08-04, and it overturns a finding this project reported twice as measured. The rule was 'a character LoRA at 0.85 destroys the setting' - observed on NIKA (a sunlit field became a grey void) and confirmed on TERRA (a snow forest collapsed to flat beige). BOTH OBSERVATIONS WERE REAL AND THE EXPLANATION WAS WRONG. It was never a property of LoRA strength. It was the UNCAPTIONED TAUPE BACKDROP of the turnaround being absorbed into the trigger: at high strength the LoRA reproduced its own training background over whatever place was asked for. Evidence at studio/samples/cast/terra_costume_fix/setting_grid.jpg - the v1 uncaptioned LoRA at 0.85 gives a featureless taupe void for snow_road and reduces a meadow to an arch-shaped window; the v3 LoRA, captioned and trained across two costumes, holds a real forest with depth and a real meadow at THE SAME 0.85 and the same seed. CONSEQUENCE: 0.85 is not inherently unsafe, and 0.5 was a workaround for a dataset defect rather than a law. The default stays 0.5 because that is what the rest of this character's evidence was measured at and nothing has yet shown 0.85 to be BETTER - only that it is no longer destructive. Any future character trained from an uncaptioned single-backdrop turnaround will reproduce the same defect, so caption the backdrop.
identity_correction: CORRECTED 2026-08-04 BY THE USER'S EYE, and it overturns this card's own earlier claim. I reported that the trained LoRA carries her with the danbooru name STRIPPED from the prompt - that she is a cast member rather than a prompt trick. THAT WAS WRONG. It was read off a small column in terra_lora_check.jpg and was too generous. On the full-body sheets the pattern is unambiguous and the user identified it unprompted: in costume_ab.jpg rows 1 and 2 are HER and rows 3 and 4 are not, and the variable between them is the NAME, not the LoRA version - v1 and v2 both hold with full tags and both fail without the name. Same in costume_recaptioned.jpg: row 1 name-stripped is not her, row 2 full tags is. WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: the danbooru tag and the LoRA are COMPLEMENTARY and the tag is load-bearing. Without the name she becomes a generic green-haired woman in a long gown - the headpiece, the asymmetric fringed sarong and the specific bodice all go. The LoRA refines and stabilises what the name summons; it does not replace it. CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY SHOT: keep 'terra branford (final fantasy vi)' in the prompt. Her provenance stays known_partial and this sharpens what that means - partial is not a half-measure to be trained away, it is a permanent dependency on the tag.
realism_verdict:
MEASURED 2026-08-04. REALISM IS A LADDER AND THE TWO HALVES TAKE DIFFERENT ROUTES. REAL LIFE works on the qwen edit path through her PHOTOGRAPHIC sheet - real wool and raw silk, a real stone hall with a real light shaft, hair that reads as hair. Evidence studio/samples/cast/terra_realism_ladder.jpg rungs 1-2. BUT THE LADDER COLLAPSED IN THE MIDDLE: rungs 1,2,3,4 came back nearly identical. The Qwen-Edit reference sheet pins the MEDIUM as hard as it pins the identity, so asking it for a 3D animated feature or an oil portrait returns the same photograph. This is the same suppression IPAdapter does on the anime path, in a new place, and it means the qwen edit route CANNOT produce semi-real. SEMI-REAL WORKS ON THE ILLUSTRATION ENGINE instead: danbooru name + trained LoRA at 0.5 + a painterly or CG style, IPAdapter at 0.0. Evidence studio/samples/cast/terra_semireal.jpg - oil, concept art, pre-raphaelite and cgi all land as visibly different media AND all four hold her headpiece, hair, bodice, sarong and boots. That is the route for anything between a photograph and a cel.

EXTENDED 2026-08-05. The sheet pins SURFACE as well as medium, which is a sharper statement of the same thing and is the reason the photoreal version was rejected twice: a smooth sheet cannot produce a rough photograph no matter what the prompt asks for. The corollary is the route this project should use for anything photographic - make the face on the t2i path, where the surface is real, and only then use the edit path to hold identity across shots.

ALSO MEASURED 2026-08-05, and it applies to every qwen render in this project, not just to hers: THE NEGATIVE PROMPT IS INERT ON BOTH QWEN GRAPHS. Both 13_qwen_t2i_styled.json and 14_qwen_edit_ref.json ship at cfg 1.0, the value at which classifier-free guidance stops consulting the negative branch. Proof at studio/samples/cast/terra_real/08_negtest.jpg and reproducible with `python3 studio/_tools/terra_real.py negtest`: at one seed, a negative deliberately loaded with the words this brief most depends on - 'photograph, real skin, skin pores, film grain, sharp focus, real hair' - is BYTE-IDENTICAL to an empty negative, as is the workflow default. Two consequences. The workflow default negative containing 'photorealistic, 3d render', which scripts/short.py never overwrites, is harmless rather than the defect it looks like. And every realism gain recorded here came from the POSITIVE prompt alone; nothing was bought by negative-prompt engineering, and nothing can be until somebody raises cfg.
face_quality_verdict: MEASURED 2026-08-04, studio/samples/cast/terra_face_quality.jpg, five arms at one seed with every cell cropped to the SAME head region at the SAME display size so the comparison is about face quality rather than about who stood closest to camera. THE FACE IS NOT A WEIGHTS PROBLEM. Full body (A) gives a small soft face with indistinct features - the ugly result. Upper body (B) at the same seed and the same LoRA gives a crisp detailed face with clean eyes and lineart. Raising the resolution on the same full-body composition (C, 1024x1536) recovers a good part of the difference. Raising the LoRA to 0.85 (E) changes the face BARELY AT ALL - it is indistinguishable from the control on this axis. THE ARITHMETIC BEHIND IT: at 832x1216 in a full-body frame the head is about an eighth of the height, so the face is roughly 90 pixels, and SDXL samples in an 8x-downsampled latent - that face was decided by about an 11x11 patch. No LoRA can add detail the sampler had no room to draw. Her frame_verdict already put the honest cut-off at 5_wide and most recent sheets were rendered fuller than that. THE FIX ORDER: frame closer, or raise resolution, or add a face-detail pass. Arm D attempted the detail pass and MY COMPOSITE BROKE IT - the re-rendered crop came back but the feathered paste-back washed it out, so D is my bug rather than a negative result. The primitives for a proper one exist on this box: SDPoseFaceBBoxes, CropByBBoxes and VAEEncodeForInpaint.
photo_face_verdict:
MEASURED 2026-08-04, studio/samples/cast/terra_photo_face.jpg, four arms at one seed on the qwen edit path. THE PHOTOREAL FACE IS THE SAME PROBLEM AS THE ANIME ONE: pixels, not model and not weights. The current three-quarter-body framing (A) gives a small soft face. CLOSE FRAMING ALONE (B) fixes it - real skin texture, catchlight in both eyes, individual hair strands - on the SAME 7.5-second path with nothing else changed. Dropping the Lightning LoRA and running 20 steps at cfg 2.5 (C) is marginally cleaner than B and takes 55.8 seconds, which is SEVEN TIMES the cost for a difference you have to hunt for. Not worth it. Arm D rendered the same close prompt with NO reference sheet and produced a good face belonging to A DIFFERENT WOMAN, which is the sheet doing exactly the job it exists for. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SHEET ITSELF: sheet_photo_terra.png is currently a three-quarter-body image, so everything conditioned on it inherits a small face. A photographic sheet should be a CLOSE PORTRAIT - the sheet teaches the face, and a sheet whose face is 90 pixels teaches a 90-pixel face.

AMENDED 2026-08-05 by studio/_tools/terra_real.py. Two things above are now out of date and one was read only half way.
- The framing claim is superseded: sheet_photo has been a face+body composite since 2026-08-04 and is now the v2 composite.
- ARM D WAS ALSO A POSITIVE RESULT AND WAS NOT SCORED AS ONE. It is the only cell in that strip with real skin, because it never went through the edit path. Read that way it says the sheet transmits its SURFACE, not only its identity and its medium - which is why v2's face panel is made on the t2i path and never round-tripped.
- THE FACE DETAIL PASS NOW WORKS AND ITS PASTE-BACK IS CLEAN. The previous attempt (arm D of terra_face_quality.jpg) produced a good crop and a washed-out merge. Two changes fix it: the re-rendered crop is colour-matched back to the original per channel on mean and standard deviation, and the feather is a narrow ring at the border instead of a soft blend across the whole crop. Checked at 1:1 on the seam, evidence studio/samples/cast/terra_real/07_facepass_seams.jpg - no edge, no level shift. It is only worth running on a face that is actually soft: on a v2-derived render at denoise 0.25 and 0.35 the 4x upscale leaves a faint lattice, and at 0.50 the pass starts inventing detail (it added a nose stud). Use 0.35, and do not make it a default.
sheet_photo_note:
WHAT THE 121-RENDER SWEEP ACTUALLY MEASURED, and three of the four results contradict something this card used to say.
1. LIGHT IS THE STRONG VARIABLE AND GRADE IS NEARLY INERT. Six lighting-and-lens treatments at one seed produced six visibly different photographs. Five film-stock and grade treatments at one seed - Portra, CineStill 800T, bleach bypass, teal-orange, Ektachrome - changed the background and a little contrast and left the face essentially alone. Spend the prompt on where the light is, not on what it was shot on.
2. GREEN HAIR DOES NOT RETURN A WIG. This card previously recorded that naming the hair green on a photoreal model gets a wig, and that it therefore had to be named as dye with roots. Measured across five hair treatments at six lights: 'a saturated deep green, long and loose' returned convincing dyed hair in all six lights. The wig in the very first sheet came from the whole cosplay sentence - gold dress, red cape, red boots, flat frontal light - not from the word green. The saturated form is now used, because it is the one that still reads as HER.
3. EXPRESSION AND GAZE ARE REAL AND CHEAP. Six treatments at one seed gave six different people-in-a-moment: laughing with the eyes creased, a tired half-smile, caught mid-turn before the eyes arrive, exhausted and unfocused. This is the fix for renders that read lifeless, and it costs nothing. It belongs on the SHOT, not on the sheet - the sheet keeps a level neutral gaze so it teaches the face rather than a mood, and the probes confirm the sheet does not impose its expression on anything conditioned on it.
4. THE RIBBON IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT FROM THE PHOTOREAL SHEET. Rendered explicitly at four seeds (03_finals_ribbon_REJECTED.jpg) as 'a narrow oxblood grosgrain ribbon tied at the crown', it comes back as a large satin gift bow with long tails sitting on top of her head - the governing rule of this project biting again, the model renders nouns. It reads as costume and it undoes the wardrobe work. Her photoreal version has no ribbon and that is a decision, not an oversight. The anime path is unaffected and keeps its headpiece.
5. A THIRD PANEL DOES NOT HELP. A bust panel was added to make the collar legible for close shots. The edit path refused the framing, returned another standing figure, and invented a gold necklace, so the three-panel sheet was two near-duplicates and a prop. Two panels, face and three-quarter figure.
